To create a journal entry about stress management, I'll use the plan from Trial #1 and Trial #2. I'll start by brainstorming a list of potential stress management techniques and then craft a journal entry that incorporates one or two of these strategies in a realistic and engaging way. 

Here's an example of a journal entry:

"Last semester, I was struggling to keep up with my coursework and felt overwhelmed with stress. I was constantly worrying about upcoming exams and assignments, and it was affecting my sleep and mood. One day, I decided to try time-blocking, where I broke down my study sessions into 90-minute increments with 10-minute breaks in between. I scheduled specific times for studying, exercising, and relaxing, and it really helped me stay focused and in control. By the end of the semester, I felt more confident and in charge of my academic life."

I came up with this example by thinking about a common stress scenario that college students might face (struggling with coursework), and then describing how a specific stress management technique (time-blocking) helped me cope with it.
